title: AWS Glue and ETL
description: Build ETL pipelines with Glue crawlers, Data Catalog, and serverless Spark jobs.

data.text: AWS Glue is a fully managed ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) service that makes it easy to prepare and load data for analytics. Glue automatically discovers your data, stores metadata in a central catalog, and generates ETL code so you can focus on your data, not the infrastructure.

A **Glue crawler** connects to your data store (S3, RDS, DynamoDB, etc.), progresses through a prioritized list of classifiers to determine the schema for your data, and then populates the **Glue Data Catalog** with metadata. The Data Catalog is a persistent metadata store — like a data dictionary — that makes your data searchable and queryable.

Glue ETL jobs transform and move data between data stores. Jobs can be written in Python or Scala using Apache Spark. Glue Studio provides a visual interface for creating ETL jobs without writing code. Jobs can be triggered on a schedule, on demand, or by events.

data.title: AWS Glue ETL Job Script (Python/Spark)
data.content: A Glue job that reads from S3 and writes to RDS:
data.code:
import sys
from awsglue.transforms import *
from awsglue.utils import getResolvedOptions
from pyspark.context import SparkContext
from awsglue.context import GlueContext
from awsglue.job import Job

args = getResolvedOptions(sys.argv, ["JOB_NAME"])
sc = SparkContext()
glueContext = GlueContext(sc)
spark = glueContext.spark_session
job = Job(glueContext)
job.init(args["JOB_NAME"], args)

dyf = glueContext.create_dynamic_frame.from_catalog(
    database="my_database",
    table_name="raw_sales",
    transformation_ctx="dyf",
)

mapped_dyf = ApplyMapping.apply(
    frame=dyf,
    mappings=[
        ("order_id", "string", "order_id", "string"),
        ("amount", "double", "amount", "double"),
        ("order_date", "string", "order_date", "date"),
    ],
    transformation_ctx="mapped_dyf",
)

glueContext.write_dynamic_frame.from_jdbc_conf(
    frame=mapped_dyf,
    catalog_connection="my-rds-connection",
    connection_options={"dbtable": "sales_analytics", "database": "analytics"},
    transformation_ctx="datasink",
)

job.commit()

data.title: Glue Features
items: **Job bookmarks** — Track processed data so you only process new or changed data on subsequent runs
**Triggers** — Start jobs on a schedule, on demand, or when another job completes
**Glue Studio** — Visual ETL editor for building jobs without code
**Glue DataBrew** — Visual data preparation tool for cleaning and normalizing data
**Glue Schema Registry** — Manage and validate Avro schemas for streaming data

terms.definition: Extract, Transform, Load — the process of moving data from sources to destinations.
A Glue component that scans data stores and infers schemas.
A central metadata repository for all your data assets.
A Glue feature that tracks processed data to avoid reprocessing.
An event that starts a Glue job — on a schedule, on demand, or on completion of another job.
A visual interface for creating ETL jobs in Glue.

items.question: Does Glue use Spark?
items.answer: Yes, Glue ETL jobs run on Apache Spark. Glue handles the Spark infrastructure for you, so you don't need to manage Spark clusters.

items.question: What is a Glue job's runtime?
items.answer: Glue jobs run in a serverless Spark environment. You only pay for the compute resources consumed during the job run.

items.question: Can Glue read from any data source?
items.answer: Glue supports S3, RDS, DynamoDB, Redshift, and many third-party databases via JDBC connectors.

points: Glue crawlers automatically discover and catalog your data schemas
The Data Catalog provides a unified view of all your data
ETL jobs transform and load data using serverless Spark
Job bookmarks and triggers automate incremental processing
data.takeaway: Glue removes the operational burden of ETL. Start with a crawler to catalog your data, then build ETL jobs to transform and move it.
